article.headline: England Storms Rawalpindi for High-Stakes ODI Tri-Series Clash Against Pakistan
article.summary: England faces Pakistan in the second match of the 50-over tri-series following the hosts' opening 37-run win over Sri Lanka.
article.body: Salman Ali Agha powered Pakistan to a confident start on Sunday, smashing an unbeaten 107 off 90 balls to help his side defend a total of 305 against Sri Lanka. The pace attack completed the job, bowling out their opponents for 268 to secure a 37-run victory at the beginning of the tournament. This momentum places significant pressure on the visiting English side as they prepare to face the hosts at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium. England coach Brendon McCullum noted the team must adapt quickly to subcontinent conditions, acknowledging that playing against local teams on their home ground requires a distinct strategic approach rather than a fixed process. Captain Harry Brook echoed these sentiments, emphasizing that his squad must be ready from the very first ball. The tri-series serves as crucial preparation for next year’s 50-over World Cup, with England entering the contest riding a wave of three consecutive ODI series victories throughout 2026. However, the visitors face the challenge without key personnel, as Jos Buttler remains sidelined by injury and Jofra Archer has been rested for this tour. The format features a double round-robin stage where each team plays the others twice. The performance of both squads in Rawalpindi will be vital in determining who secures one of the top two spots required to qualify for the final scheduled for October 31 in Lahore.

article.headline: موجة صعود جديدة ترفع سعر الدولار ليلامس 54 جنيهًا في البنوك المصرية
article.summary: سجل الدولار الأمريكي اليوم الثلاثاء 20 أكتوبر 2026 سعرًا يتراوح بين 53.88 و54.02 جنيه في البنوك المصرية.
article.body:
مع بدء تداولات اليوم الثلاثاء 20 أكتوبر 2026، سجلت أسعار الدولار مقابل الجنيه المصري تحركًا جديدًا نحو الصعود، حيث بلغ السعر في البنك المركزي المصري 53.88 جنيه للشراء و54.02 جنيه للبيع، مما يعكس حصيلة تقلبات السوق خلال الساعات الماضية.

تعد هذه الأسعار مؤشرًا هامًا للمتعاملين في الأسواق والمهتمين بأسعار الصرف، حيث تختلف معدلات الشراء والبيع بشكل طفيف بين المؤسسات المصرفية المختلفة، مما يحدد التكلفة النهائية لعمليات التحويل أو التعاملات التجارية المرتبطة بالعملة الصعبة.

وفقًا لبيانات "اليوم السابع"، سجل سعر الدولار في البنك الأهلي المصري وبنك مصر 53.89 جنيه للشراء مقابل 53.99 جنيه للبيع. بينما قدم البنك التجاري الدولي، وبنك البركة، والمصرف المتحد، وبنك قناة السويس سعر 53.90 جنيه للشراء مقابل 54.00 جنيه للبيع. كما سجل بنك الإسكندرية 53.92 جنيه للشراء و54.02 جنيه للبيع، في حين استقر السعر في بنك الكويت الوطني عند 53.89 جنيه للشراء و53.99 جنيه للبيع.

تأتي هذه التحركات في ظل مراقبة مستمرة لحركة العملات الأجنبية في السوق المحلية، حيث كانت التعاملات السابقة قد شهدت ارتفاعات في أسعار عملات أخرى مثل اليورو والجنيه الإسترليني والفرنك السويسري، وذلك بالتزامن مع التقارير الواردة في "بوابة أخبار اليوم" حول تأثير التوترات الإقليمية على استقرار الأسواق المحلية. وتستمر فروع البنوك وشركات الصرافة في المواقع الحيوية كالمطارات والمولات والمدن السياحية في العمل وفقًا للسياسات النقدية المعتمدة لاستيعاب احتياجات المواطنين والقطاعات المختلفة خلال هذه الفترة.

news.og_title: Gold falls as dollar, Treasury yields rise; silver holds modest gains - Kitco PM Report
news.og_desc: (Kitco NewsWire) - Spot gold prices were lower and spot silver prices were slightly higher in late U.S. trading Monday, as a firmer U.S. dollar and rising Treasury yields pressured bullion while traders weighed persistent inflation risks against expectations for a Federal Reserve pause later this month. A rebound in technology stocks reduced some defensive demand for gold, while continued uncertainty surrounding the Strait of Hormuz limited selling pressure across precious metals. At the time of writing, spot gold was trading near $4,137.80 an ounce, down $26.30, or 0.63%, while spot silver was trading near $56.930, up $0.068, or 0.12%.North American equities closed mixed as technology shares rebounded from last week's sharp selloff. The S&P 500 rose 31.29 points, or 0.4%, to 7,690.73. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 36.38 points, or 0.1%, to 51,966.03. The Nasdaq Composite gained 290.85 points, or 1.1%, to 26,430.89, while the Russell 2000 added 6.93 points, or 0.3%, to 2,728.30. Technology and semiconductor shares led the recovery as investors reassessed concerns about financing costs and capital spending associated with artificial intelligence infrastructure. In Canada, the S&P/TSX Composite fell 247.92 points, or 0.7%, to 35,928.63, weighed down by financial and metal-mining shares.European equities finished sharply lower after weekend protests in France and Italy renewed concerns about government finances, borrowing costs and political stability. The Stoxx Europe 600 declined 0.80% to 639.56. France's CAC 40 fell 1.11% to 7,868.05, Germany's DAX lost 1.18% to 25,319.77 and the U.K. FTSE 100 dropped 1.08% to 10,764.69. Italy's FTSE MIB declined 1.55% to 49,086.27. French government bond yields climbed as investors demanded additional compensation for sovereign risk, while weakness in the euro provided some support for the U.S. dollar.Market positioning remains focused on the divergence between slowing employment growth and persistent inflation. September CPI rose 0.6% on the month and 3.7% annually, while producer prices climbed 1.3% on the month and 6.3% from a year earlier. September retail sales increased 0.8%, indicating continued consumer resilience despite elevated borrowing costs. Futures markets put the probability of an October Fed rate increase in the mid-teens, leaving a pause at the Oct. 27-28 meeting as the base case, while the probability of additional tightening in December remained close to 90%. The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield rose to approximately 5.135%, reversing part of last week's bond-market rally and increasing pressure on non-yielding gold. China's third-quarter economic growth accelerated to 4.5% year over year from 4.3% in the second quarter, supported by exports, although domestic consumption and property investment remained weak. The next major U.S. economic tests are Tuesday's housing starts and pending home sales, Thursday's weekly jobless claims and Friday's preliminary purchasing managers' indexes and final October consumer sentiment. Softer activity and employment data would support gold through lower yields, while resilient demand and elevated inflation expectations would reinforce December tightening risk.The Strait of Hormuz and U.S.-Iran situation remains a major source of energy-market uncertainty, even as oil futures retreated from recent highs Monday. President Donald Trump's decision to waive some newly imposed sanctions and tariffs affecting Russian energy exports raised expectations for additional fuel supplies, but shipping disruptions in the Middle East continued to constrain the market. Iranian forces have been linked to renewed attacks on commercial vessels around Hormuz, while Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis claimed additional attacks against Saudi energy and military facilities. The latest Houthi claims had not been independently confirmed. Crude shipments through Hormuz remain below prewar levels, and the absence of a durable U.S.-Iran agreement continues to support a geopolitical risk premium. December Brent crude settled at $109.55 a barrel, down 0.3%, while December WTI settled at $98.54, down 0.5%. The expiring November WTI contract rose to $103.66 amid thin trading. For gold, geopolitical uncertainty remains supportive of defensive demand, but elevated energy prices continue to threaten higher inflation expectations, Treasury yields and a stronger dollar.The key outside markets see December Nymex WTI crude oil prices lower and settled near $98.54 a barrel, while December Brent crude settled near $109.55. The yield on the benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury note is trading near the 5.14% area.
